literal: welcome (from the Arabic root for spaciousness)
usage: Used to welcome guests into a home, customers into a shop, or anyone arriving at a location. It is universally understood across all regions of Morocco and suits both formal and casual situations. Hosts often repeat the word multiple times in rapid succession to emphasize their hospitality.

variants.label: to one person
variants.note: Add 'bik' to direct the welcome specifically to a single individual.

variants.label: to a group
variants.note: Used when welcoming two or more people at the same time.

variants.label: emphatic
variants.note: Used by hosts to show immense hospitality and warmth to arriving guests.

examples.english: A thousand welcomes, make yourself at home (the house is your house).
